item.title: Zhipu’s Chinese Founder Says Frontier AI Should Stay Open to All
item.description: The founder of Chinese AI lab Zhipu argued that frontier artificial intelligence should remain broadly accessible rather than controlled by select individuals, weighing in on a growing debate about the risks posed by ever more powerful models.

item.title: China EVs on Road Have Average Age of 1.8 Years, Newspaper Says
item.description: Chinese electric vehicles on the road are on average just 1.8 years old, compared with 8.2 years for gasoline-powered cars, 21st Century Business Herald reported, citing a report by the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers and Hejun Consulting.

item.title: Typhoon Bavi Weakens as Heavy Rain Spreads Across China
item.description: China’s National Meteorological Center said Typhoon Bavi weakened to a severe tropical storm on Sunday morning after making landfall in Zhejiang.

item.title: Korea’s World-Beating Stocks Are Now Trading Cheaper Than Ever
item.description: South Korea’s blistering stock rally has left investors facing an unlikely backdrop: equities trading at record-low valuations.

item.title: Modi Courts Indo-Pacific Partners as China, US Reshape Region
item.description: From missiles and uranium to critical minerals and sports diplomacy, Prime Minister Narendra Modi used a three-nation tour to deepen India’s Indo-Pacific partnerships as regional powers strengthen ties amid China’s growing influence and uncertainty over US engagement.

item.title: Warsh and US Inflation Will Set Tone for July Fed Decision
item.description: Kevin Warsh is about to make his first appearance before Congress as Federal Reserve chairman, and during two days of testimony he’ll have new US inflation data to parse with lawmakers.

item.title: Banks’ Record Bond Short Sparks Quest for Answers
item.description: For the first time in recent history, primary dealers have gone net short on debt they used to hold billions of dollars of.

item.title: Homes Are in Short Supply in the US. How a New Law Could Change the Market
item.description: A new law adopted on July 11 marks the most significant effort in decades to boost the US housing supply.

item.title: Help Not Wanted: World Cup Hiring Boost Has Yet to Materialize
item.description: The hiring boom the FIFA World Cup was expected to bring to the US looks like it may not end up materializing after all.

item.title: OpenAI Engineer’s ‘LOL’ Moment Set Stage for Legal Fight With Apple
item.description: When iPhone engineer Chang Liu quit for a job at OpenAI’s nascent hardware division, Apple Inc. says he left with more than just years of experience.

item.title: Fuel Prices Are Slamming Consumers Even as Crude Crisis Fades
item.description: Prices for gasoline, diesel and jet fuel are rebounding even as crude oil eases, a rare divergence that’s swelling costs for peak-season travelers and threatening to undermine President Donald Trump’s pledge to quash inflation ahead of midterm elections.

item.title: Stocks Priced for ‘Sunshine and Rainbows’ Now Face Earnings Test
item.description: Wall Street is anticipating a near-record earnings season, but for investors a key question remains: Will it be enough to keep stock market bulls running?

item.title: Fed Task Force Picks Bring Credibility and Support for Warsh
item.description: The external advisers Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh tapped to lead the central bank’s five new task forces lend credibility to his efforts to rethink how the institution communicates and implements policy, according to economists and analysts who follow the Fed closely.

item.title: The World’s First Trillionaire and the Company He Won’t Let Go
item.description: Elon Musk made history last month.

item.title: EasyJet Has Private Equity Firms Going Out of Their Comfort Zone
item.description: The aviation industry has seen plenty of deals activity in recent years, but the battle between two US funds for EasyJet Plc stands out because the volatile, low-margin airlines business rarely draws financial suitors.

item.title: Vietnam’s Paramount Leader To Lam Has a Grand Vision for His Nation
item.description: The World Bank just elevated the country to “upper-middle” income status. But he’s got bigger plans.

item.title: China Tells Refiners to Keep Fuel Output High as Iran War Drags
item.description: China instructed some major refiners to keep fuel production high, according to people familiar with the matter, in an effort to protect domestic consumers as strikes in the Persian Gulf once again threaten oil shipments.

item.title: Charting the Global Economy: Iran War Continues to Cloud Outlook
item.description: The outlook for the global economy grew more uncertain this week as tensions flared between the US and Iran.

item.title: Eni’s Descalzi Says Energy Crisis May Worsen in Short Term: Sole
item.description: The global energy situation could deteriorate further as oil inventories decline and competition for supplies intensifies, Eni SpA’s Chief Executive Officer Claudio Descalzi told Italian daily Il Sole 24 Ore.

item.title: China Power Load Hits Early Record as Data, EV Demand Rises
item.description: China’s nationwide electricity load reached a record high for the first time this year on July 10, hitting 1.518 billion kilowatts, the National Energy Administration said in a statement posted on its official WeChat account Saturday.

item.title: VW CEO Under Pressure as Labor Unions Torpedo Turnaround Plan
item.description: Volkswagen AG Chief Executive Officer Oliver Blume faces an uphill battle to push through a fundamental overhaul of the carmaker after failing to win initial backing from the supervisory board.

item.title: Xi Says China’s Backing for Kim and North Korea Won’t Change
item.description: President Xi Jinping said China’s commitment to its friendship with North Korea, support for Kim Jong Un’s leadership and determination to safeguard the two countries’ common interests “will not change,” Xinhua News Agency reported on Saturday.

item.title: Kazakh Tycoon Turlov’s Freedom Raises $300 Million for Expansion
item.description: Kazakhstan billionaire Timur Turlov’s Freedom Holding Corp. raised $300 million in a share sale to help fund its ongoing international expansion.

item.title: OpenAI Safety Head Heidecke to Leave Firm After Reshuffle: Wired
item.description: OpenAI head of safety Johannes Heidecke is leaving the artificial intelligence company following a reorganization, according to Wired.

item.title: India, NZ Plan Strategic Partnership Including Maritime Security
item.description: India and New Zealand will elevate their relationship to a “strategic partnership,” as both seek closer trade and security ties.

item.title: MGM Resorts Engaged in Deal Talks With Diller, WSJ Says
item.description: MGM Resorts International is engaged in deal talks with Barry Diller’s People Inc. after the entertainment mogul offered to acquire the part of the casino company he doesn’t already own, the Wall Street Journal reported.

item.title: Hedge Fund Elliott Builds Stake in Software Firm CCC
item.description: Elliott Investment Management has built a large stake in car-insurance software provider CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc., which has been exploring a potential sale, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: SK Hynix Debut Is a Bet That AI Breaks Boom-and-Bust Chip Cycle
item.description: South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix Inc. just pulled off the largest public listing by a foreign company in US market history. Shares soared 13% on their first day of trading.

item.title: Nuclear Energy Services Firm Holtec Joins Sector’s IPO Rush
item.description: Holtec Nuclear Corp. filed for a US initial public offering, becoming the latest in the sector to try to capitalize on data centers’ growing power demands.

item.title: Rhode Island Jail Operator Files Bankruptcy to Cut Bond Debt
item.description: Central Falls Detention Facility Corp., which houses federal detainees including people arrested by the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, filed for bankruptcy saying it cannot afford to keep paying on more than $167 million in bond debt.
